answer: Using logistic regression with Age as the sole predictor (statsmodels sm.Logit, unregularized MLE, fitted on all 80 clean patients; target = Efficacy=='PR' with PR=41, PD+SD=39), the predicted probability of achieving efficacy PR at Age = 65 is **0.3952** (≈39.5%). Model: intercept 4.4466 (SE 1.451), Age coefficient −0.0750 (SE 0.024, p=0.002), converged=True, pseudo R²=0.097, LLR p=0.0011. Caveat (known, per the mandated single-predictor spec): Efficacy is perfectly confounded with Groups (Group 1 treatment = 100% PR, Group 2 = 0% PR), so the Age-only model implicitly mixes both trial arms; the estimate is a model-based value over the 40–75 age range (only 5 patients are exactly age 65), not a local observed rate.
